case_name: Kazakhstan Aral Sea Restoration AI Monitoring
problem_solved: The Aral Sea (shared by KZ and UZ) shrank to 10% of its original size due to Soviet-era irrigation diversion. The North Aral Sea (KZ side) partially recovered after the Kokaral Dam (2005) but required continuous environmental monitoring: water level, salinity, biodiversity, and dust storm frequency. Manual monitoring was infrequent and expensive. AI satellite analysis enabled continuous environmental change detection.
architecture_summary: Satellite change detection platform: Sentinel-1 (SAR) + Sentinel-2 (optical) + Landsat time series for water surface monitoring. Change detection algorithm: NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index) time series analysis with anomaly detection. Air quality monitoring: MODIS aerosol optical depth for dust storm detection from dried seabed. Biodiversity: drone survey AI for vegetation and bird population counting. Data portal: public-access dashboard showing water level trend, salinity estimates, dust storm frequency. World Bank co-funded component for UZ Southern Aral.
outcome_metrics: Continuous water level monitoring: North Aral at 1-week update frequency. Dust storm prediction accuracy: 78% for 48-hour advance warning. Biodiversity survey: 45 bird species confirmed returning to North Aral. Annual environmental reporting: cost reduced 70% vs field surveys. Data shared with IFAS (International Fund for Aral Sea Saving — all 5 CA countries).
failure_modes: SAR satellite analysis requires specialist geophysicist interpretation — technical skills shortage in regional environment agencies. Cross-border data sharing with UZ: restricted on some datasets for sovereignty reasons. Dust storm predictions insufficient for agriculture planning (need 5-day advance warning).
replicability_factors: All satellite data is free (Copernicus). Algorithm published in ISPRS and RSE journals. IFAS coordination mechanism exists for CA-wide rollout. World Bank Environment project funding available.
uz_transferability_rationale: UZ is the most directly affected country by Aral Sea disaster (Southern Aral dried completely). Satellite monitoring of Southern Aral dust storms is a PUBLIC HEALTH PRIORITY (Karakalpakstan respiratory disease rates are 3x national average from dust exposure). World Bank NSDI project includes environment monitoring component. IFAS provides multilateral framework. Budget: included in existing World Bank projects — incremental cost is $1-2M for AI analytics layer.
kg_transferability_rationale: KG's environmental monitoring priorities are different (mountain glacier retreat, lake level changes, forest degradation) but the satellite monitoring architecture is identical. Issyk-Kul lake monitoring, Tien Shan glacier retreat tracking, and Toktogul reservoir level monitoring are all achievable with the same AI satellite analysis pipeline. Budget: $2-4M for KG environmental AI monitoring. UNDP, GEF, ADB environment projects.
key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language environmental monitoring dashboard. Integration with national hydrometeorological service data. Extension of dust storm prediction to 5-day window (requires better NWP model). Public access dashboard for civil society and media (transparency requirement).

problem_solved: Rotterdam (90% below sea level) needed to plan and monitor climate adaptation infrastructure (green roofs, water squares, permeable pavements, underground storage) across the city. Different departments maintained separate data on infrastructure, land use, and climate risk with no integrated view for planning or emergency response.
architecture_summary: Rotterdam Climate Digital Twin: FIWARE (open-source IoT platform) aggregating sensor data from 200+ rain gauges, 500+ water level sensors, 1,200+ environmental sensors. 3D city model (CityGML format) with overlay of flood risk zones, green infrastructure coverage, and heat island intensity. AI modules: flash flood prediction (4-hour advance warning, ML on sensor + NWP data), urban heat island mapping (ML on temperature sensors + satellite), green infrastructure performance measurement. Open data portal: all sensor data publicly accessible. Policy application: developers must show digital twin impact assessment for new buildings.
outcome_metrics: Flash flood early warning: activated 12 times, 0 false alarms in pilot period. Urban heat reduction measurement: green infrastructure verified 2.3°C reduction in pilot district. Building permit assessment: 500+ new buildings screened via digital twin. Climate investment prioritisation: $180M in city infrastructure spending optimised via digital twin modelling.
failure_modes: FIWARE platform complexity: open-source flexibility comes with integration complexity — required 18-month technical build. High sensor density cost ($28M hardware + platform). 3D city model requires continuous update — 5-year data staleness creates planning errors. Private landowner green infrastructure not captured (only public land monitored).
replicability_factors: FIWARE is free open-source. Rotterdam Climate Centre publishes case studies. Applicable to Tashkent and Bishkek where flash flooding and heat island are documented urban risks.
uz_transferability_rationale: Tashkent summer temperatures (45°C peak in 2024) create urban heat crisis. Flash floods in Ferghana Valley are a seasonal hazard. Rotterdam's sensor network + flash flood warning is directly applicable. Start with flash flood early warning (highest urgency) then add heat island mapping. Budget: $5-8M for Tashkent urban climate monitoring pilot. Donor pathway: ADB urban, World Bank DRM, GEF.
kg_transferability_rationale: Bishkek faces both flash flooding (debris flows from Ala-Too mountains) and heat island effects. Rotterdam's architecture is applicable at Bishkek city scale for $4-6M. The mountain-city flash flood model (different dynamics from Rotterdam sea-level flooding) requires adaptation. UNDP urban resilience programmes are donor pathways.
key_adaptation_required: Adaptation for mountain flash flood dynamics (different from Rotterdam coastal flooding). Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language public dashboard. Open data policy for sensor data. Urban planning regulation requiring digital twin assessment for new construction.

case_name: India ISRO Bhuvan Geoportal & Environment Monitoring
problem_solved: India needed a national geospatial platform for environment monitoring, forest cover change detection, land degradation assessment, and disaster management that used India's sovereign satellite data (Resourcesat, Cartosat) rather than relying on international commercial providers. Bhuvan provided a Google Earth equivalent operated by ISRO with Indian satellite imagery.
architecture_summary: National web GIS platform: Bhuvan portal (bhuvan.nrsc.gov.in) with Indian satellite imagery archive (15+ years), vector datasets, and analysis tools. Environment modules: forest cover change detection (bi-annual), land degradation assessment, wetland mapping, coastal change monitoring, Aral Sea equivalent (Chilika Lake seasonal mapping). AI layer: automated change detection between time-series imagery, forest encroachment alert system, crop yield estimation from satellite. API: open access for government agencies, researchers. Disaster Management Support (DMS): real-time flood and cyclone mapping during events.
outcome_metrics: 15TB+ of satellite imagery accessible to government users. Forest change detection: 98% of India's forests mapped bi-annually. 10,000+ government users. Disaster response: cyclone Fani (2019) — flood mapping updated every 6 hours. Forest encroachment alerts: 5,000+ alerts issued to forest departments. India's land degradation atlas produced using Bhuvan data cited in IPCC reports.
failure_modes: Commercial satellite imagery quality: ISRO satellites have lower resolution (5.8m) than commercial providers (0.3m) for some applications. User interface dated — adoption low among non-specialist users. Cross-ministry data silos: Forest, Agriculture, Disaster ministries maintain separate Bhuvan instances with no unified view. Cloud processing added late — initial architecture was batch downloads only.
replicability_factors: Bhuvan open architecture published by ISRO. Developing countries can access Indian satellite data under bilateral agreements. ESA Copernicus provides equivalent free satellite data globally. This architecture is the reference for building a sovereign geo-analytics platform without commercial satellite dependency.
uz_transferability_rationale: UZ World Bank NSDI project ($35M, 2025-2030) is building exactly this — a national spatial data infrastructure. Bhuvan architecture + ESA Copernicus data (free) is the technical foundation. The AI change detection modules for cotton field monitoring, Aral Sea monitoring, and land degradation are directly applicable. Budget is covered by WB project — additional AI analytics layer is $2-3M incremental cost.
kg_transferability_rationale: KG needs environment monitoring for glacier retreat, deforestation in Fergana range, and pasture degradation. Bhuvan architecture using free Copernicus data is feasible for KG at $3-5M. GEF and World Bank environment projects are funding sources. Key application: pasture degradation monitoring for KG's 9M cattle/sheep.
key_adaptation_required: Use ESA Copernicus data (globally free) rather than Indian ISRO satellites. Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language geoportal. Adaptation of change detection algorithms for CA landscapes (Central Asian steppe vs Indian tropical/semi-arid). Integration with national hydrometeorological services data.

case_name: China BeiDou Navigation + Environmental Monitoring in Central Asia
problem_solved: China promoted BeiDou satellite navigation as a GPS alternative across BRI partner countries. In Central Asia, BeiDou-based applications were deployed for agricultural monitoring, flood early warning in mountain areas, and infrastructure monitoring along the Karakoram Highway and China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan rail corridors.
architecture_summary: BeiDou III constellation (2020 fully operational): precision navigation + SMS capability + short-message emergency service for remote areas without cellular coverage. CA applications: (1) Agricultural IoT: BeiDou-connected soil sensors for precision farming along BRI agricultural zones; (2) Slope stability monitoring: BeiDou GNSS displacement sensors on mountain slopes along CKU (China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan) planned rail route; (3) Fleet management: BeiDou tracking for cross-border transport. No cellular coverage required — BeiDou provides direct satellite communication link.
outcome_metrics: BeiDou used in UZ precision agriculture pilots: 15,000 ha with BeiDou-connected sensors. Slope monitoring: 200 critical slope sites monitored along planned CKU rail corridor. Emergency SMS: field workers in Tien Shan mountains (no cellular) using BeiDou for distress messaging. CA coverage: all of UZ and KG covered with BeiDou signal.
failure_modes: Geopolitical sensitivity: Western donors discourage BeiDou adoption in CA projects they fund (sanctions risk for US-listed components). Data sovereignty: BeiDou applications route some telemetry data via Chinese ground stations. Device supply chain: BeiDou-enabled devices sourced from Chinese manufacturers only.
replicability_factors: BeiDou provides free civilian positioning service globally. For remote CA areas without GPS/cellular coverage, BeiDou emergency messaging is the ONLY option. The agricultural monitoring architecture is vendor-neutral if BeiDou is used as positioning layer only.
uz_transferability_rationale: BeiDou is ALREADY in use in UZ. The monitoring applications (agriculture IoT, slope stability) are relevant. However, Western donor projects will not procure BeiDou-primary systems. Score 6: medium transferability with geopolitical caveat. UZ can use BeiDou for applications funded without Western donor restrictions (national budget, IsDB, AIIB, EDB).
kg_transferability_rationale: Same caveat. KG remote mountain areas where GPS accuracy is poor and cellular is absent — BeiDou emergency messaging is the only option. Slope monitoring along CKU rail corridor is a Chinese-funded project that naturally uses BeiDou. Score 6 with same geopolitical asterisk.
key_adaptation_required: Data sovereignty protocol — ensure BeiDou telemetry does not route through Chinese state servers. Use BeiDou positioning layer with sovereign data storage. Avoid BeiDou for applications where Western donor restrictions apply.

case_name: Finland Aurora AI — National AI Strategy for Public Services
problem_solved: Finland needed to apply AI systematically across government services, particularly in areas where Finland has competitive advantage: forestry management, cold-climate agriculture, and environmental data analytics. The Aurora AI programme identified 150+ government AI use cases and piloted the highest-priority ones across 10 government agencies.
architecture_summary: Government AI coordination programme: Aurora AI task force under Prime Minister's Office identifying AI opportunities across all ministries. Key environmental implementations: (1) MAVI satellite-based agricultural subsidy verification (replacing field inspections); (2) Forestry AI: drone + satellite analysis of forest health, illegal logging detection; (3) Helsinki environmental twin (building permit environmental impact AI). Technical platform: Azure Government for most AI deployments. Open AI register: Finland publishes list of all government AI systems (algorithmic transparency). AI ethics board reviews all citizen-facing AI.
vendors_involved: Finnish Transport and Communications Agency Traficom
outcome_metrics: 150 AI use cases assessed; 20 in production by 2021. MAVI agricultural subsidy AI: 400,000 field inspections replaced by satellite verification, saving €35M/year. Forestry drone monitoring: 3M hectares monitored annually at 20% of manual cost. Government AI register: 40+ systems published publicly. Finland ranks global top-5 for government AI readiness.
failure_modes: Voluntary AI ethics review: 30% of agencies skipped review. Azure Government dependency creates commercial lock-in. Some AI systems implemented without adequate training data (low-data rural areas). Public sector workers resisted AI workload tools fearing job displacement.
replicability_factors: Finland publishes AI register publicly — methodology replicable. MAVI satellite subsidy verification architecture directly applicable to UZ cotton subsidy fraud detection. Nordic Council of Ministers has co-funded AI programme replication in Baltic and Arctic states.
uz_transferability_rationale: Finland's MAVI agricultural subsidy satellite verification is the MOST DIRECTLY APPLICABLE component for UZ: $35M/year savings from eliminating field inspections maps proportionally to $100M+/year potential for UZ cotton subsidies. The forestry AI is applicable to UZ's Uzbekistan afforestation programme (Yashil Makon). Budget: $3-5M for UZ satellite subsidy verification (agriculture component). Finland's open AI register concept is a governance good practice UZ could adopt for trust-building.
kg_transferability_rationale: Finland's forestry drone monitoring is applicable to KG's deforestation crisis in Fergana range and Chui Valley. The open AI register transparency model is directly applicable — KG Цифровой Кодекс (2025) includes provisions for AI accountability. Budget: $2-4M for KG environmental AI monitoring. Nordic-Baltic cooperation channel provides diplomatic pathway.
key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz language AI system interfaces. Open AI register adapted to CIS legal context. Avoid Azure dependency — sovereign cloud compliance required for UZ/KG government systems. Adaptation of forestry models for Central Asian vegetation types (juniper forest vs Finnish boreal).

case_name: Kyrgyzstan GLOF (Glacial Lake Outburst Flood) Early Warning System
problem_solved: Kyrgyzstan has 2,000+ glacial lakes fed by 8,000+ glaciers in the Tien Shan. Glacial retreat (accelerating at 0.8%/year) is increasing GLOF events — sudden, catastrophic floods from glacial lake outbursts that destroy downstream villages with minutes of warning. The KG Hydromet Service needed automated lake monitoring and early warning to give downstream communities 30+ minutes notice.
architecture_summary: UNDP/GEF funded pilot: satellite lake area monitoring (Sentinel-2 time series, lake area growth anomaly detection), 30 high-priority lakes instrumented with GPS-tracked shore sensors + acoustic water level gauges. AI module: lake area + inflow rate change detection triggering alert, downstream flood routing model (using DEM + HydroSHEDS drainage basin data). Alert propagation: SMS alerts to ayil aymak (local government) and village Telegram groups. Integration with KG Hydromet national early warning system.
outcome_metrics: 30 high-risk lakes monitored continuously. GLOF event detected and warned: 3 events 2021-2023, all with 45+ minutes advance warning (vs 0 previously). No casualties in monitored areas during those events (vs 12 deaths in unmonitored comparable events in same period). Phase 2: expanding to 100 lakes planned.
failure_modes: Sensor power in remote areas: solar panels at 4,000m elevation have limited winter generation. Satellite cloud cover during storm events (exactly when GLOFs occur) reduces detection reliability. Alert propagation to non-smartphone communities requires multiple channels. False alarm rate: 3 false alarms in 3 years creating community fatigue.
replicability_factors: This IS a KG case — demonstrates donor-funded environmental AI at small scale. Architecture is replicable for any mountain country with glacial lake hazard. Directly relevant to UZ (Fergana Valley receives water from KG mountains) as shared risk.
uz_transferability_rationale: UZ Ferghana Valley receives floodwaters from KG mountain GLOF events — UZ is a downstream stakeholder in KG's GLOF warning system. Bilateral data sharing: KG GLOF alerts should automatically trigger UZ downstream alert for Ferghana communities. Budget: $1-2M for UZ downstream alert integration with KG GLOF system. World Bank DRM project funding.
kg_transferability_rationale: This IS a KG case — Phase 2 expansion to 100 lakes is the ACTIVE PROCUREMENT. The Phase 2 sensor network, satellite monitoring platform, and community alert system expansion is a $15-20M procurement. GEF, UNDP, World Bank DRM project are potential funders. This is one of the most urgent and directly actionable cases in the KG portfolio.
key_adaptation_required: Phase 2 adaptation: satellite cloud-penetrating SAR (Sentinel-1) as primary detection during storm events. Community alert via Telegram + radio (not just SMS). Power reliability: fuel cell backup for remote sensors. Kyrgyz language alerts.

case_name: New Zealand MfE AI Emissions Reporting
problem_solved: New Zealand's Ministry for the Environment (MfE) needed to improve greenhouse gas inventory accuracy, especially for agricultural emissions (methane from livestock — 50% of NZ's GHG). AI-assisted satellite and sensor data analysis could improve agricultural emission estimates beyond traditional activity-based calculations.
architecture_summary: Multi-source emissions monitoring: agricultural CH4 estimates using satellite methane column measurements (TROPOMI Sentinel-5P), livestock density maps (from aerial survey + ML), land use change detection. Urban emissions: traffic emissions AI using vehicle counts × emission factors × congestion multipliers. Industrial: automated reconciliation between industry-reported data and satellite NO2/SO2 measurements for anomaly flagging. All integrated into NZ Greenhouse Gas Inventory system. Public dashboard: real-time emissions tracking by sector/region.
outcome_metrics: Agricultural emissions estimate uncertainty: reduced from ±15% to ±8%. Anomaly detection: 3 industrial facilities flagged for under-reporting (regulatory action taken). NZ GHG Inventory quality: upgraded from Tier 1 to Tier 2/3 for 60% of emission categories. Public dashboard: 50,000+ monthly users tracking regional emissions.
failure_modes: TROPOMI satellite resolution (7km) insufficient for point-source attribution in dense agricultural areas. Cloud cover over NZ's hilly terrain reduces satellite measurement frequency. Industry-reported data quality highly variable — some sectors self-report inaccurately without penalty.
replicability_factors: TROPOMI satellite data is free (Copernicus). Architecture applicable to any country needing Paris Agreement-compliant GHG monitoring. Central Asian agricultural methane (cotton and livestock) is a specific application.
uz_transferability_rationale: UZ has livestock and cotton agriculture emissions that are poorly quantified. Paris Agreement reporting requires improved GHG inventory. NZ architecture using free TROPOMI data is applicable for $3-5M. Donor pathway: GEF, ADB climate finance. Key: UZ GHG reporting accuracy is needed for accessing climate finance (carbon credit markets, green bonds).
kg_transferability_rationale: KG has significant livestock methane emissions (9M livestock) and hydro power sector (which has its own reservoir methane emissions). Paris Agreement reporting improvement. Donor pathway: GEF, World Bank. Budget: $2-3M.
key_adaptation_required: Russian/Uzbek/Kyrgyz interface. Adaptation for cotton agriculture emission factors (not in NZ model). Integration with national statistical system for activity data. Climate finance (carbon credit) market connection to monetise emission reductions.
